name: Tsukuyomi, Moon Order Lord
loreTies: Tsukuyomi embodies moon order, ritual distance, night law, and cold precision within The Sacred Kingdoms.
The Torii-Moon Gate allows this deity to enter Ascension-era dungeon routes without collapsing the individuality of other Realms.
Kami culture, symbols, weapons, and divine law shape every ability, artifact, silhouette, and combat choice.
shortBackstory: Tsukuyomi, Moon Order Lord, is a playable god in Mythos Gates: Ascension. Tsukuyomi is the true source-realm divinity behind the mythology — moon order, ritual distance, night law, and cold precision. Ascension expands divine power during the current Gate crisis; it does not turn a mortal into a god.

chapters.title: Divine Origin
chapters.text: Tsukuyomi is not a mortal hero inspired by myth. Tsukuyomi is the actual god recognized by Kami source culture, born from the supernatural laws of The Sacred Kingdoms. Their domain — moon order, ritual distance, night law, and cold precision — determines their symbols, weapons, posture, combat instincts, and relationship to sacred authority.

chapters.title: Faction Bond
chapters.text: Within Kami, Tsukuyomi expresses the civilization rather than merely representing it. Their visual identity must carry the materials, beauty standards, divine symbols, and sacred rules of The Sacred Kingdoms. Their gameplay role, Battery, must grow from mythology first and mechanics second.

chapters.title: Mythos Gate Wound
chapters.text: During the Ascension era, Tsukuyomi can interact with The Torii-Moon Gate because divine beings are intrinsically connected to their Realms. The Gate does not become a simple teleportation portal; it is a mysterious boundary where separate mythological realities become traversable. Tsukuyomi understands some rites of crossing, but not the complete origin of the Mythos Gates.

chapters.title: Dungeon Role
chapters.text: When selected by the player, Tsukuyomi enters the dungeon alone as one god or goddess against multiple enemies. No army follows. No squad shares control. Every room, trap, shrine, relic, elite, and boss encounter must test how moon order, ritual distance, night law, and cold precision survives pressure from creatures, rival Realm laws, and unstable Gate conditions.

chapters.title: Ascension Conflict
chapters.text: Ascension is the current story arc, not the permanent end-state of the Mythos Gates universe. For Tsukuyomi, Ascension means restoration, awakening, evolution, or expansion of existing divine power. Their personal conflict is to recover strength without reducing Kami mythology into raw fuel for the crisis.

relationshipHooks: Faction witnesses interpret how Tsukuyomi crosses The Torii-Moon Gate.
Rival deities challenge the limits of cross-Realm travel.
Dungeon lore pickups reveal Gate mystery without resolving the full origin.
developmentStatus: Playable deity backstory aligned to Mythos Gates identity, one-deity dungeon runs, current Ascension arc, and preserved Lore Codex canon.
mythicSource: source culture humans later copied as Japanese myth and Shinto shrine lore
visualCanon: Sayo is a shrine-cartographer who maps living thresholds. Her ink, mirror charms, shide seals, cedar tools, foxfire lanterns, and quiet ritual posture should feel like the source of later shrine mapmaking and spirit folklore.

mythosGatesCanon.identityRule: Tsukuyomi is the actual god of Kami source mythology, never a mortal hero or generic champion.
mythosGatesCanon.arcRule: Ascension restores, awakens, evolves, or expands existing divine power; it does not make the character a god for the first time.
mythosGatesCanon.mysteryRule: The backstory may reveal how this deity interacts with the Mythos Gates, but must not resolve the full origin of the Gates.
